require_first_item_under_heading.heading: boildown
require_first_item_under_heading.matching: ^\s*the work of this session is now on\s*:
require_first_item_under_heading.why: The Boildown opens with where the work is and which of the five stages it finished -- "The work of this session is now on: <branch> (you have finished step N of 5, <Stage>)" -- in every reply, a plan-only one included (no branch yet, step 1 of 5, Consider).

why: Morgan, 2026-09-29 (strength: decided): the first bullet after the Boildown heading names the branch this session's work is on and the stage it has finished, with no exception. Blocking, like the heading beside it, because it is structural: the line is either first under the heading or it is not, and a line meant for every reply is the kind a session drops when the rest of the reply feels finished.

_examples.reply:
Done.

## Boildown
- The work of this session is now on: staging (you have finished step 3 of 5, Booked).

require_in_fence_paired_with.why: a paste block that tells another session to land, merge, push or open a pull request onto staging or main, or says the same in other words (a stage word as the order, make it live, ship it, merge the PR, --promote, gh pr merge, git push origin main) carries landing authority, and only the person's own Booked (or Approved, Go update) for this handoff gives it -- quoted in the block, so the receiving session can check it. Without that word, the prompt ends at Act: build on the feature branch, push it there, and stop

why: 2026-10-01: two prompts a session wrote ended 'Land it on staging per this repo's conventions'. Morgan had not said Booked, and routine work then landed on the tier below staging, never on staging. fence-block-for-paste passed both, because it checks that a block says where it goes, not what it authorizes. Morgan: 'No, we always want to do it in the local container ("Act") and then I'll authorize it to go to pre-staging via "Promote" etc.' 2026-10-08: a block that ends at the feature branch may NARRATE a past landing (a session or tool did it, past tense, no 'you') without being read as an order (BestPractice tools/precedent_reply_check.py, narration_exempt_if_block_matches). Later on 2026-10-08: the trigger skipped any LINE holding do not/never/no/without, so 'Merge it into main, no questions asked' passed with nobody's Booked. A negator now exempts a clause only when it governs the landing verb in that clause (BestPractice tools/precedent_reply_check.py, negation_exempt_if_clause_negates), and also_if_matches lists the other ways a block says land. Morgan: 'shouldn't it understand the intent behind commands not just the literal words?' (practice: read-for-intent, BestPractice). 2026-10-10: a block asking for a workflow fix said the step "fires on a pull request into main" -- a description of the event, not an order -- and was refused. A clause whose every landing phrase follows a preposition and an article ("on a", "after every") is forgiven (BestPractice tools/precedent_reply_check.py, description_exempt_if_clause_preceded_by); the verb makes the order, so "Open a PR into main" is still judged. An engine older than that ignores these keys: it judges every negated line, the stricter reading, and enforces if_matches alone. 2026-10-10, later: this rule says "inherits": true, so universal's own copy supplies every key not set here. The narration, negation and description exemptions are still stated here too, because an engine older than "inherits" reads only this copy and would otherwise lose them; drop them once every repository runs BestPractice 24f06d0 or later. Newer exemptions (the quoted-output one) come from universal alone (BestPractice tools/precedent_reply_check.py, _settle). An engine older than that replaces outright and lacks those exemptions: stricter, never looser. 2026-10-20: the pair read descriptions as orders ("merge the PR" as one example in a bracketed list, and a quoted report that "--land refused a direct push to staging"), so every verb-led trigger now counts its verb only where it is addressed to the reader -- a line or clause start, or after then, please, you, can, must and the like -- and not as a non-final item of a bracketed list of examples, and the stage word not where it is named "as an instruction", while commands (--promote, gh pr merge, --base, git push) stay orders wherever they stand (Morgan, 2026-10-20: "2 use your judgment"). 2026-10-29: the pair now states only what it adds -- landing_branches, the stage-word and --promote triggers in adds_if_matches, its quoted Booked and its Act narration -- and inherits every other trigger and exemption from universal's pair, widened to these branches (BestPractice tools/precedent_reply_check.py, _inherit_pair, 16e89051a). An engine with "inherits" but older than _inherit_pair reads universal's triggers for main alone, without staging or the stage words; one older than "inherits" reads no trigger at all. So this trim lands only once every repository that brings this set runs _inherit_pair.

Paste into: a new session rooted in o/r.

```

```

Paste into: a new session rooted in o/r.

```
Fix it, then land it on staging, as he said: "Booked".
```

why: Morgan, 2026-10-09: "I want to make sure there's a full check *somewhere* on the push to main, afterwards" -- with four exceptions: GitHub's test runs on it, Debut passed on exactly this, only prose changed, or he asked for a fast one. A merged fast move that owes the full local suite on main holds the turn until it has started, and while it has failed.

The archive-line reply and the closing reply link the branch cleanup page, only when there is something on it (Morgan, 2026-10-05), and refresh it only when the person says "Branch cleanup" (Morgan, 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-27), by writing its rows into the page's own database (2026-10-27). The gate runs this set's tool and prints its note before the reply; it moved out of BestPractice's reply gate on 2026-10-17 (BestPractice spec/ENFORCEMENT_LIVES_WITH_ITS_PRACTICE_PLAN.md part 3). Printed only, never evaluated: an engine older than that day reports note_from_tool as a key it does not know, until Update Vendors.

require_finished_plan_asks_to_act.heading: boildown
require_finished_plan_asks_to_act.plan_words: \b(?:plan it|brainstorm|write it up|spec it out|one-line plan|(?:the|this|my|a|our) plan(?! of record))\b
require_finished_plan_asks_to_act.tell: \bI(?:'|’)?m (?:already |now )?(?:acting on|carrying out) (?:this|the|that|my) plan\b|\bI am (?:already |now )?(?:acting on|carrying out) (?:this|the|that|my) plan\b

why: Morgan, 2026-10-30 (strength: decided): "if a session has just considered or made any sort of plan, then upon the completion of the plan, it needs to ask or tell me to see if I want to implement the plan." Universal's the-boildown rule (boildown-finished-plan-asks-to-act) reads a plan as finished when the turn wrote a plan file or added a **Plan:** line; this adds the ladder's own reading, a first Boildown line naming the Consider step while the reply makes a plan, which only a person who brings the ladder writes. Moved here from BestPractice's reply_check.json on 2026-10-31, where the engine's set-words-stay-in-their-set refused the step label in universal's rules.
